source.extractionNote: Third pass. Two corrections from the second pass: (1) the icon-swap resolver used in earlier passes read only the swapped node's own variant name (e.g. 'Style=rounded') instead of walking up to its parent COMPONENT_SET name (the actual glyph identity) — fixed by a targeted re-read, which reversed three previously-reported 'placeholder icon' blockers (see issues). (2) a direct read of the nested initials TEXT node across all nine Size variants confirms its fontSize scales proportionally with Size (root ÷ 3, only medium token-bound) — not previously covered. Master set (9 size variants) plus 4 on-page subcomponents extracted in full (_Avatar Swatch, _Avatar Type, _Status Indicator); _Avatar Photos sampled at 3 of 40 named variants (content input, not API). Node id 4906:1172 (from the second pass) still current.

summary: A visual representation of a user or entity, shown as a photo, initials, or icon, with an optional status indicator. Nine sizes step from xxxsmall to xxxlarge with medium as the base, and the badges, ring and glyphs all scale from that step. The status badge carries a distinct glyph per state as well as its colour. Content type isn't an exposed property, swap the nested Avatar Type instance directly to change it. For a notification count on an icon or nav item, use the Notification Indicator component instead, Avatar's own indicator is for presence, not counts.

intent.xxxsmall: The smallest step, for dense inline contexts like compact tables or comment threads. The presence glyph is only a few pixels across here, so do not rely on anyone reading it.
intent.xxsmall: A step up from xxxsmall, still compact, for dense lists.
intent.xsmall: For secondary avatars in tight layouts, like a stacked group of collaborators.
intent.small: For list rows and menu items where the avatar sits alongside text.
intent.medium: The base step, and a balanced general-purpose choice for cards and list headers. Every other size is scaled from it, so start here unless something specific argues otherwise.
intent.large: For emphasis in a card header or a comment's author avatar.
intent.xlarge: For a prominent single avatar, like a user menu or account switcher.
intent.xxlarge: For profile headers where the avatar is a focal point.
intent.xxxlarge: The largest step, for full profile pages or standalone display. The close glyph does not grow with its badge at this size, so check it still reads as a target.

intent.true: Shows a dismiss badge pinned to the top-right corner. Use in removable contexts, like a multi-select chip list.
intent.false: Hides the dismiss badge. The default for most read-only contexts where the avatar isn't removable.

intent.true: Shows a presence badge pinned to the bottom-right corner, defaulting to Available. The badge is described in the metadata as 'an exposed instance... reachable in the properties panel without detaching' — not supported by this extraction, see issues.
intent.false: Hides the presence badge. Use when presence doesn't apply, like a generic entity avatar or a purely illustrative photo.

intent.true: Shows a border/default outline ring around the avatar, weight scales with Size.
intent.false: Hides the ring. Use on backgrounds where the outline competes with surrounding content.

internalVariations.intent: Initials, photo, or icon. Not an exposed property, swap the nested Avatar Type instance directly to change it.
Background color behind initials or an icon, using chart/series tokens. Not used behind a photo. Swap the nested Swatch instance directly.

The metadata's Content & Slot table now calls this 'exposed nested instance, 8 states... reachable from Avatar's own properties panel without detaching'. Avatar's own componentPropertyDefinitions has no such property (only Size, Show Close, Show Status, Show Ring) — this extraction still finds it swap-only. See issues. Each of the six presence states binds a genuinely distinct, verified glyph (confirmed by resolving the icon swap's parent component set, not just its own variant name): Available→available, Away→away, Busy→busy, DND→dnd, On Shift→on-shift, Offline→offline. Close is the exception — see issues, it currently points at the same glyph as Offline, which reads as a Figma authoring bug rather than intended reuse.

options: any icon component (INSTANCE_SWAP), Figma default resolves to the glyph 'star' (component 'Star', verified in packages/icons and not in that build's rejected list)
internalVariations.intent: Only meaningful on the Status Indicator's own Status=Icon variant. Both the on-page instance and the property's own default resolve to the 'Star' component ('star' glyph) — the metadata's Property Breakdown stating Default 'Star' is accurate. It's still described as if it were an Avatar-level property, which it isn't (Avatar's own componentPropertyDefinitions has no Custom Icon entry — see issues).

contentInputs.note: Sample photo library (named after people), not an enum — 40 named variants, 3 extracted as a representative sample.

sizing.h: fixed at every size except medium, which is fill

anatomy.role: Fills the frame, auto-positioned. Holds initials with a colored swatch, a photo, or an icon with a colored swatch. Not an exposed property, swap the nested instance directly

Surrounds the avatar's content circle from outside its edge — border/default color, stroke only, drawn proud of the content rather than overlapping it. Weight scales proportionally with Size, 2px at medium.

stroke.width: stroke/thick at medium only (token-bound); every other size is an unbound raw value equal to rootWidthPx ÷ 24 — see variants table and issues

anatomy.note: Confirmed intended rendering: the ring sits outside the avatar's content, not inset over it. Figma's own raw geometry (re-verified) draws the Ring ellipse at the exact same box as the content, with strokeAlign=INSIDE — which, taken literally, overlaps the outer rim of the photo/swatch rather than surrounding it. Implement per the confirmed intent (ring expands outward from the content circle) rather than the literal raw alignment; see issues.

anatomy.role: Pinned to the top-right corner. An instance of the Status Indicator component's Close variant, shown or hidden with Show Close. Like every _Status Indicator instance, it has a foreground/inverse border ring (the void layer) around its fill, badgeSizePx ÷ 16 thick at every size — see the _Status Indicator subcomponent anatomy.

Pinned to the bottom-right corner, defaults to Available. Shown or hidden with Show Status. The instance is exposed, so its state, and for the Icon state its glyph, are reachable directly. Like every _Status Indicator instance, it has a foreground/inverse border ring (the void layer) around its fill, badgeSizePx ÷ 16 thick at every size — see the _Status Indicator subcomponent anatomy.

variants._note: root.sizePx is measured, not a token, except at medium where root.widthToken applies. badge.sizePx = root.sizePx ÷ 3 exactly at every step (an internally consistent formula the metadata does not state correctly — see issues). ring.weightPx = root.sizePx ÷ 24 exactly at every step; only medium's ring weight happens to also be represented by a real token (stroke/thick). initials.fontSizePx = root.sizePx ÷ 3 exactly at every step too (same ratio as badge.sizePx, independently verified by reading the nested initials TEXT node's own fontSize inside each Size variant) — only medium's fontSize happens to also be token-bound (label/large/font size = 16px).

anatomy.ref: Icon (shared library component, not one of this page's subcomponents)
anatomy.note: Name#2167:166 INSTANCE_SWAP resolves to the 'Verified' component (glyph 'verified', confirmed present in packages/icons/codepoints.json and not in that build's rejected list) — a real, specific default glyph, not a placeholder.

subcomponents.name: _Avatar Photos

name.type: string (sample content, not a real enum)

subcomponents.note: 40 named photo variants = a content input (image source), never modeled as an enum in code. Only 3 sampled during extraction per the skill's sampling rule for large content sets.

customIcon.note: Confirmed by resolving the swap to its parent component set, not just its own variant name. Matches the metadata's stated default ('Star') exactly.

anatomy.role: A full-badge-size background circle, present and visible behind every status, not only Offline. Creates a border/halo effect: fill inset by exactly badgeSizePx ÷ 16 sits on top of it, so this ring shows all the way around at every size. Only its colour changes (Offline only).
The presence-colour circle, inset from the badge edge by exactly badgeSizePx ÷ 16 at every size (measured ratio, not a token) — this inset is what reveals the void ring as a border around it.

anatomy.note: Each status swaps a genuinely distinct, verified glyph via Name#2167:166 (confirmed by resolving to the swap target's parent component set) — see the variants table's glyph column. Size/Framed properties and position constraints are otherwise unchanged per status.

table.glyph: offline — see issues, likely a Figma authoring bug; the intended glyph is presumably 'close'

states.whatChanges: Avatar has no hover, pressed, or focus states in Figma. Close and Status are static badges that change only with the Status property, so whatever click behaviour Close has in a real interface lives in code rather than here.

behavior.description: None modeled in Figma. Avatar is presented as a static graphic, any transition when swapping Size, content, or toggling Show Close, Show Status, or Show Ring lives in code.

content.description: Initials, photo, or icon. Not an exposed property, swap the nested Avatar Type instance directly to change it.
Background color behind initials or an icon (purple, blue, sea, yellow, orange, green, burgundy, using chart/series tokens). Not used behind a photo. Swap the nested Swatch instance directly.
Used only when Content type is photo, fills the circle. In Figma swap the nested Photo instance to any of the named photos in _Avatar Photos. In code any image can be passed as an image property.

Holds one of eight states from the _Status Indicator component, each drawn with its own glyph from the Assets library. The instance is exposed, so the state is set from Avatar's own properties panel without detaching. Only rendered while Show Status is true.
The glyph used while Status is Icon. Any component can be swapped in and the suggested list holds only the Star set, so nothing constrains it to a presence-shaped mark.

do: Match Size to context, dense lists and tables call for the smaller sizes (xxxsmall to small), profile headers and standalone display call for the larger ones (xlarge to xxxlarge).
Turn off Show Status for generic entities or purely illustrative photos where presence doesn't apply.
dont: Don't use the presence Status badge for unread or notification counts, that's a different purpose, use the Notification Indicator component instead.

accessibility: Purely visual, an avatar image or initials alone don't convey a name, pair it with visible text or provide an accessible name in code

Each presence state now carries its own glyph as well as its colour, so the badge no longer depends on colour alone. Still give it a text equivalent, because at the smallest sizes the glyph is only a few pixels across
The Close badge implies a dismiss action, give it an accessible name in code like "Remove [name]", Figma has no interactive state for it
The close glyph is drawn at a fixed size whatever the avatar, so on the largest avatars it sits very small inside its badge. Check it still reads as a target

layoutTheming.type: Fixed per Size, medium is the base
layoutTheming.description: Nine fixed squares stepping 24, 32, 36, 40, 48, 64, 80, 120 and 200px, with medium at 48px as the base. Medium is the only step bound to a token (control/lg), every other step is an authored value. Not resizable independently of the Size property.

layoutTheming.type: Scales with Size, medium is the base
layoutTheming.description: The Status and Close badges are 16px at medium, exactly one third of the avatar, and step 8, 10, 12, 12, 16, 18, 24, 36 and 56px across the ladder. Above medium they grow more slowly than the avatar, so a large avatar is never dominated by its badge.

The status glyph holds a constant share of its badge at every size, 0.42 of the badge width, so it stays proportional from 24px through 200px. The close glyph is drawn at a fixed 5px at every size, so its share of the badge falls from two thirds at xxxsmall to under a tenth at xxxlarge.

layoutTheming.type: Scales per Size tier, medium is the base
layoutTheming.description: 2px (stroke/thick) at medium and every step below it, 4px (stroke/heavy) at large and xlarge, then 6px and 8px at xxlarge and xxxlarge. The two heaviest weights are authored values rather than tokens.

Pinned flush to the top-right and bottom-right corners, inset by exactly the badge's own width so both sit inside the avatar's bounds at every size. They scale in position as the avatar resizes and do not move independently.

Ring uses border/default. Each status draws its circle from a chart token, chart/positive for Available, chart/negative for Busy and chart/series steps for the rest, with the glyph on foreground/inverse. Offline inverts that pair, a foreground/inverse circle carrying a foreground/secondary glyph. Swatch colours use chart/series. All resolve separately for light and dark mode.

visualReference.policy: No images are stored; every node deep-links into Figma so a shot can be pulled on demand and is never stale.

issues.detail: The Property Breakdown and Content & Slot table now document 'Status' (8 states) and 'Custom Icon' as if they were properties reachable directly on Avatar — one calling Status an 'exposed nested instance... reachable in the properties panel without detaching'. Avatar's actual componentPropertyDefinitions has only 4 properties (Size, Show Close, Show Status, Show Ring); no Status or Custom Icon property exists at the Avatar level. Both remain swap-only on the nested _Status Indicator subcomponent in this extraction. Either the exposure described in the metadata hasn't been applied in Figma yet, or the metadata is describing an aspirational API — a developer following the metadata literally would look for a prop that doesn't exist.

The Close status variant's icon swap (Name#2167:166) resolves to the same glyph node as Offline (component 'Offline', id 4769:8596) rather than a dedicated dismiss/close icon. Every other status has its own correctly-matched glyph (see the _Status Indicator variants table), which makes this look like a copy-paste oversight on that one variant rather than intended reuse. A faithful implementation would render an 'offline' glyph on the dismiss badge, which is almost certainly wrong — recommend using the verified 'close' glyph (packages/icons has it) for the Close badge instead of reading it off this swap.
Layout & Theming Intents states Size steps at '24, 32, 36, 40, 48, 64, 80, 120 and 200px'. The extracted rootWidthByOption for 'large' is 60px, not 64px — every other step matches.

Layout & Theming Intents states badge sizes step '8, 10, 12, 12, 16, 18, 24, 36 and 56px' and that they 'grow more slowly than the avatar' above medium. The extracted Close/Status badge boxes are instead exactly root width ÷ 3 at every single size (8, 10.67, 12, 13.33, 16, 20, 26.67, 40, 66.67) — a flat proportional ratio, not a slowing one, and numerically different from the stated list at small and above.

Layout & Theming Intents states ring weight is '2px (stroke/thick) at medium and every step below it, 4px (stroke/heavy) at large and xlarge, then 6px and 8px at xxlarge and xxxlarge.' The extracted stroke weights instead scale continuously as root width ÷ 24 at every step (1, 1.33, 1.5, 1.67, 2, 2.5, 3.33, 5, 8.33) — below medium the weight is under 2px, not flat at 2px, and large/xlarge measure 2.5/3.33px, not 4px. Only medium's weight (2px) happens to coincide with a real token (stroke/thick); no size uses stroke/heavy or any other token.

Root width is bound to control/lg only in the medium variant; ring strokeWeight is bound to stroke/thick only in medium. Every other size's root width and ring weight are unbound raw values (consistent with the proportional-scale finding above, and consistent with Layout & Theming's own separate statement that 'medium is the only step bound to a token').
_Avatar Type's initials text fill is a raw #ffffff with no token or style.
space/none's token description states '= 32px, source: scale/10' but resolves (primitives.scale.0) to 0px.
control/lg's token description states '= 56px, source: scale/15' but resolves (primitives.scale.15) to 48px.

Every glyph named in this spec (available, away, busy, dnd, on-shift, offline, verified, star, and the recommended close) is confirmed present in packages/icons/codepoints.json by exact figmaName match and absent from that build's rejected list.

Earlier passes resolved every INSTANCE_SWAP componentProperty (icon swaps) by reading only the swapped node's own name — which for a variant member is just its variant string (e.g. 'Style=rounded'), not the parent component set's name that actually identifies the glyph. This produced three false 'placeholder icon, no glyph committed' blockers, all now retracted: Avatar's own Icon content type (real default: 'Verified'), Status Indicator's Custom Icon default (real default: 'Star', confirmed to match the metadata), and the presence status icons (each genuinely distinct, not identical). Fixed by re-resolving each swap's parent COMPONENT_SET name directly. Any other spec produced by the same extraction approach that reports an icon swap as an unresolved placeholder should be treated as suspect until re-verified the same way.

Accessibility and Layout & Theming both describe a 'close glyph' fixed pixel size (stated as 5px) inside the Close badge. This extraction stops at the Close/Status instance boundary by design (subcomponent internals are read from _Status Indicator directly, not re-walked per Avatar size), so the claim could not be verified against Avatar-scaled geometry — worth a targeted follow-up read if precise per-size icon sizing matters.
Content type, swatch color, status, and custom icon are all swap-only in this extraction (see the blocker above re: the metadata's 'exposed' claim). Decide in code whether any become real props.

The master component set's on-page default content type changed since the prior extraction pass in this session (previously rendered as Icon content by default, now renders as initials, matching _Avatar Type's own default variant).
States & Triggers and Behavior & Motion Intent are both explicitly 'none modeled' in the metadata — intentional, not missing.

issues.source: Figma geometry vs confirmed design intent
issues.detail: A direct re-read of the Ring ellipse across all nine Size variants confirms its bounding box is identical to the avatar's own content box at every step, with strokeAlign=INSIDE — meaning the raw Figma geometry draws the ring stroke overlapping the outer rim of the photo/swatch, not surrounding it from outside. Design has confirmed the intended rendering is a ring that sits outside the content circle (see the ring anatomy entry). Implementers should follow the confirmed intent, not the literal Figma alignment; this file's Ring node itself was not corrected (per this skill's read-only principle — any fix belongs in Figma).

The metadata's Anatomy and States sections frame Offline as 'the one hollow badge' via its void layer, implying void/border is Offline-specific. A direct re-check across sizes shows the void layer is actually a full-badge-diameter background circle present and visible on every status, with fill (the presence colour) inset from the badge edge by exactly badgeSizePx ÷ 16 at every size — this produces a visible foreground/inverse border ring around every status and the Close badge, not only Offline. Only the void layer's colour changes for Offline (to foreground/secondary), which is what makes that one read as 'hollow' — the underlying two-layer (void + inset fill) structure is universal. Confirmed by measuring Fill/Void boxes directly at xxxsmall, medium, and xxxlarge (ratio holds exactly at all three).
